Libya Herald (2020, reporting on a 2020 ICC arbitration ruling) independently corroborates the same timeline, describing the Tripoli-Khoms and Khoms-Mellitah pipeline projects as still under construction when Libya's 2011 revolution halted work. Together these two independent sources support a 2010 construction/commissioning window consistent with ConstructionYear=2010, though again describing the broader corridor rather than a distinct 25km segment.

Punj Lloyd's retrospective (Yumpu p.54) states the Tripoli-Melita Gas Pipeline distributes 'approximately 200 MMSCFD' through the new 34-inch line. 200 MMSCFD converts to ~2.07 bcm/yr (200 x 365 x 0.0283168), a close match to the stated Capacity=2.00 bcm/y (~3% off, consistent with rounding of an approximate figure). This is the only source found with a capacity figure in directly comparable units; OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 does carry a 'Capacity' column for these lines but in units (1,000 scm/yr) that appear to represent cumulative lifetime throughput rather than a nameplate annual rate (values in the tens of millions, i.e. tens of bcm, implausible as an annual rate for a single trunk line) -- did not use it as corroboration because the metric isn't clearly the same thing. Only one strong source found within session search budget (web search was rate-limited/CAPTCHA-walled partway through this shard; DDG, Bing, Ecosia, Mojeek all failed after initial queries) -- tier medium, independent=false pending a second source.
